name: n4_read_history
description: Read the last records of one history, newest first, to prove records arrive (a {ok} history extension proves it runs, not that records exist). Name the history by history_id (/<station>/<history name>, as historyConfig.id shows it) or by ext_ord (the history extension's ORD, e.g. station:|slot:/Folder/Point/NumericInterval, resolved to its id with one BQL select); give exactly one; a bare name (no '/') is a history of the connected station. Each row is {timestamp, value, status} as the station renders them (localized display text, e.g. '15 nov 2026 20:09:35 CST', '21,0', '{ok}'); columns are the station's headers. Optional range: period (today, last24Hours, yesterday, weekToDate, lastWeek, last7Days, monthToDate, lastMonth, yearToDate, lastYear) or start and/or end (BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00, or a span back from now such as 30m, 24h or 7d, sent as UTC; start no later than end), not both; range echoes the start/end sent. truncated is true when the range holds more records than limit; total_records is the range's record count (select count(*)), null with total_records_note when that count failed. summary=true answers how high (or low) it got in the same call: summary {count, complete, records_scanned, numeric, min {value, timestamp}, max {value, timestamp}, first and last {value, timestamp, status}, status_counts} over the WHOLE range whatever limit cut the rows, from one extra read of every record with machine-encoded time and value (timestamp ISO-8601 with the station's offset, value 21.0 not '21,0'; a tie keeps the earliest record). A non-numeric history (boolean, enum) has numeric false, min and max null and a note; a nan or inf record is counted but never compared. A range larger than summary_max_rows (default 100000) is summarized from its newest records with complete false, a note, and range_min/range_max from the station's select min(value), max(value) where status.null = false over the whole range (null-status records left out, as in the summary; a nan or inf record still counts there); a failed summary read is summary null with summary_note. A history that cannot be read is an error naming the id and how to list the ids. cov_hint=true (station-audits S3) suggests a COV changeTolerance from the same read (summary and cov_hint together still read once): cov_hint {suggested_tolerance, rule, records_considered, complete, deltas {count, median, p90, p99, nonzero_median, noise_floor, zero_share}, candidates [{tolerance, deltas_within, reduction}], reduction_estimate}. Rule: suggested_tolerance is the smallest value of the 1-2-5 series (..., 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, ...) at or above the nearest-rank median of the non-zero |delta| between successive records for which a simulated COV (keep a record when |value - last kept value| > tolerance, as BNumericCovHistoryExt compares) keeps at most half of the records; records with a null status or a nan/inf value are left out; noise_floor is the smallest non-zero |delta|. A non-numeric history (boolean, enum), fewer than 2 numeric records or a failed read is cov_hint null with cov_hint_note; a value that never changes has suggested_tolerance null and a note. Report only: nothing is written to the station. Read-only: fixed queries over a history: ORD, no file output (n4_export_history writes histories to a CSV).

history_id.description: History id /<station>/<history name>, e.g. /MyStation/MyPoint, or a bare history name of the connected station, e.g. MyPoint

period.description: Period id: today, last24Hours, yesterday, weekToDate, lastWeek, last7Days, monthToDate, lastMonth, yearToDate or lastYear

start.description: Range start as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00 or 2026-11-15T06:00:00Z, or a span back from now: 30m, 24h, 7d

end.description: Range end as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T23:59:59.999-06:00, or a span back from now: 30m, 24h, 7d

summary.description: true adds summary: count, min and max with their times, first, last and status counts over the whole range

summary_max_rows.description: Most records the summary reads; a larger range is summarized from its newest records and says so

cov_hint.description: true adds cov_hint: a COV changeTolerance suggested from the range's real data (report only, nothing is written)

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds
